content.question: What happens after you click Finish to create a project?

options.text: Gradle build process starts and builds the application

content.explanation: After clicking Finish, the Gradle build system starts working and begins building your application. This is an automated process that compiles your project. You need to wait until the process is completely finished.

content.question: What should you do while the Gradle build is in progress?

options.text: Wait until the process gets completed

content.explanation: While the Gradle build process is running, you should wait until it is completely finished. Do not interrupt or close the IDE during this process.

content.question: What appears on your screen once the build is complete?

options.text: An interface with various code sections

content.explanation: Once the build is complete, your screen will show an interface with various code sections and panels. Don't be afraid of this code; you will learn all of it during the course.

content.question: What should you do to clean up your workspace initially?

options.text: Close everything and minimize side panels

content.explanation: To make your workspace cleaner and more manageable, you should close unnecessary elements and minimize side panels. This helps you focus better on learning.

content.question: Where is the minimize icon located to hide side panels?

options.text: At the top of the window
At the bottom of the screen

content.explanation: The minimize icon is located on the side panel itself. You click on it to minimize or hide that panel from your view.

content.question: What folder should you click to see the app structure?

options.text: Folder icon at the top left side

content.explanation: By clicking on the folder icon available at the top left side of the IDE, you can see the app folder directory structure, which shows all the folders and files in your project.

content.question: Where should you look to find the res (resource) directory?
content.explanation: The res (resource) directory is located inside the app folder. Initially, you should expand this folder to understand the project structure.

content.question: What is commonly found in the layout folder?
content.explanation: The layout folder contains XML files that define the user interface layout. The activity_main.xml file is the default layout file for the main screen of your application.

content.question: What is an emulator in Android?

options.text: A virtual device that simulates a real Android device on your computer

content.explanation: An emulator is a virtual device that allows you to run and test Android applications on your computer without needing a physical device. It mimics the hardware and software features of a real Android device, including the operating system, sensors, and storage.

content.question: How do you stop a running application on the emulator?

options.text: Click on the square icon at the top of the emulator

content.explanation: To stop a running application on the emulator, you click on the square icon mentioned at the top of the emulator window. This will stop the application execution.
